pageCache.text:
A Special Place to Learn
Co-educational day school for pupils 4-18. Barnes, South West London
Set on a serene and secluded riverside site in South-West London, Harrodian is an inspirational place for pupils aged from 4-18 to work, play and grow up.
The natural beauty of Harrodian’s campus setting is enhanced by elegant and vivid architecture and excellent facilities custom-designed to meet the needs of four age groups – Pre-Prep, Prep, Senior, and Sixth Form – that make up a single, cohesive whole.
In this short film, Harrodians explain why they think Harrodian is 'a Special Place to Learn'.
Nurturing the Individual
Enabling every child to flourish is a central plank of our teaching philosophy
Harrodian has a mission to support every pupil to fulfil their potential, wherever their talents lead them. It’s no accident that our strong academic reputation in humanities and the arts has emerged in parallel with a record of growing achievement in Maths, Science, Economics and subjects right across the curriculum.
These excellent all-round teaching strengths are mirrored in our exciting and extensive co-curricular programme where Lego Mindstorm, Model United Nations and Debating are all booming alongside Drama, Music, Rowing and Sport of all kinds.
Educating the whole child
Educating the ‘whole child’ physically, socially and morally runs as a vital thread and guiding principle through every Harrodian’s school career.
Educating the ‘whole child’ physically, socially and morally runs as a vital thread and guiding principle through every Harrodian’s school career.
Harrodian’s holistic approach provides hands-on pastoral care, support and guidance all the way from Reception to the Sixth Form.
We set out six pillars – compassion, resilience, independence, curiosity, ambition, and inclusivity – as key values for our pupils to embrace at Prep level. We actively encourage Senior pupils both to live by these principles and to pass them on to younger Harrodians through our well-established Leadership, Mentoring and Partnership and Outreach programmes.
Cherishing the Community
Togetherness is an essential ingredient in our identity as a school.
Harrodian is a place in which warmth, spontaneity, and mutual peer-to-peer support are established as the norm.
Harrodian culture is built on teamwork and united by bonds of enduring friendship. This approach finds expression through co-curricular clubs, activities, fixtures and trips that transcend age barriers and 'whole-school' events which reinforce and celebrate the variety and vitality of our wider community.

A Special Place to Learn
Headteacher, Mr James Hooke, introduces Harrodian, reflecting on its history, the development of its remarkable site and the qualities that make it stand out as a special place to learn.
Welcome
Thank you for visiting the Harrodian website. Harrodian is a relative youngster in school terms but it has done a great deal of growing up and maturing in its first 30 years or so. When the School was established in 1993 on the site of the former Harrods Sports Club, just 65 Pre-Prep and Prep age pupils were accommodated in a single building. Today, we cater for nearly 1,040 boys and girls aged 4-18 in a single school integrating dedicated sections for Pre-Prep, Prep, Senior and Sixth Form age groups.
Enhancing the Site
I believe several key factors account for Harrodian’s growth and popularity. The first is our amazing riverside location. Always a place of natural beauty, our 25-acre site has been enhanced over the years by the addition of elegant new buildings custom-designed to suit our priorities and needs.
Superb new facilities have been added – among them science labs, ICT suites, art studios, music and drama study centres, sports pitches, a dedicated Sixth Form space and, nearby, a fully-equipped boathouse on the Thames at Putney – to create a serene and special campus in which to learn, play and grow up.
New facilities added in recent years include a dedicated Sixth Form floor and, nearby, on the Thames at Putney, a fully-equipped boathouse. ”
Bringing out the Best
Academic standards reflect the high quality of the learning environment. Working across a diverse subject range, our dynamic specialist teachers and support staff are devoted both to bringing the best out of all our pupils and to inspiring them to discover new interests and passions through participation in our extensive co-curricular programme.
Exam results are maintaining a steady, upward path with established strengths across the arts and humanities matched by excellent performance in Social Sciences, STEM subjects, and more.
The Harrodian Spirit
I believe the other quality that makes the School a special place to learn is our unique Harrodian Spirit – which you can explore further in this dedicated section of our site. Parents and children alike cherish a holistic educational culture in which kindness and help for others are viewed as vital ingredients in the mix alongside personal and collective achievement. Harrodian is a place full of spontaneity and warmth, a close-knit community bound by a strong sense of togetherness in which strong and lasting friendships are the norm.
Headteacher, Harrodian
Book a visit
You can discover more about our values and see them in everyday action by visiting the Harrodian Spirit section of this website on the links below. But to really get a sense of Harrodian you will need to visit us. Tours run by our staff will also allow you to meet the pupils themselves. They are our finest ambassadors and will be happy to provide some personal views on what makes Harrodian a special place to learn.

Welcome to Pre-Prep
Harrodian’s purpose built Pre-Prep department is a warm and close-knit environment which nurtures entry-age children into curious, enthusiastic and confident young learners.
Welcome to Pre-Prep
Welcoming younger children aged from four to eight, Harrodian Pre-Prep is just a short walk from the Prep and Senior/Sixth Form age-group departments. Ours is a positive and big-hearted learning environment where staff relish the challenge of setting children on their way to a lifelong love of learning and are committed to a strong partnership involving parents at every stage of the journey.
Pre-Prep is a positive and big-hearted environment where staff set children on their way to a lifelong love of learning”
Our approach to learning
Pre-Prep starts with a strong focus on Reading and Maths as our bedrock. Our considered and patient academic approach enables children to acquire effective learning skills so they are well-prepared to become enthusiastic and engaged pupils and creative and critical thinkers as they grow.
Pastoral Care
Our teachers and teaching assistants form the passionate heart of our pastoral and well-being programme. They are committed to growing children’s confidence, developing their essential social skills and introducing them to our Pillars: key values that they can learn to live by both at School and beyond its boundaries.
Co-Curricular
Our academic and pastoral programmes are enriched by a varied and exciting range of co-curricular activities. Among them are sports and other clubs, trips to nature reserves, parks and more, house competitions throughout the school year and lots of drama.(Find out more about our Co-curricular programme via this link).

Welcome To Prep
Harrodian Prep focuses clearly on building and honing pupils' key knowledge and skills, enabling each individual to shine, wherever their natural talents may take them.
Welcome from the Heads of Prep
The Prep School sets out to build upon the skills that we establish in the Pre-Prep. Independence, kindness and personal responsibility are further developed, with a growing focus on critical thinking and empathy for one another.
Our balanced, well-rounded curriculum provides the foundation for pupils to enter the Senior School, ready and prepared for the new challenges they face.
Joint Heads of Harrodian Prep
Our approach to learning
Our academic ethos and curriculum are designed both to impart key skills and to provide pupils in Key Stages 2-3 with diverse opportunities to explore the world.
Pastoral Care
At Harrodian we believe that a happy child learns best. The time and effort we invest in the happiness of children at every point in their school career reflects this.
Learn more about Pastoral
Co-Curricular
Harrodian’s distinctive, personally-focused educational ethos has always cherished self-expression alongside academic achievement. We view the co-curricular activities all our pupils take part in beyond the classroom as vital ingredients in their development.
The Arts
The Arts are part and parcel of Harrodian’s identity as a school. You can find out about art clubs and trips, dance and drama activities, choirs, orchestras and collaborative performing arts productions here.
Sport
Harrodian teams are increasingly on the up across all age groups and Harrodian’s Prep teams are no exception. Our well-drilled, highly motivated teams are playing better and competing more strongly year by year both in local and national competitions.

pageCache.pageTitle: Admissions | Harrodian, Independent day school, 4-18, London
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Harrodian Admissions
We understand that choosing the right school for your child is an important decision, and we are here to guide and support you every step of the way.
Admissions Overview
At Harrodian, we welcome pupils at specific year group entry points in our Pre-Prep at Reception, Lower Prep at Year 4, Upper Prep at Year 7, Senior School at Year 9 and Sixth Form. Occasional places for any other year group are subject to availability.
We look for young people who will embrace the wide range of academic, sporting, creative, and social opportunities on offer and who will bring their own unique contributions to our vibrant school community. We look forward to getting to know you and your family, and we are excited to show you what makes Harrodian such a special place.
If you have any questions at any stage, please don’t hesitate to get in touch – we’d love to hear from you. Call us on 020 8762 6321 or email us at admissions@harrodian.com
Tours & Open Mornings
Click Here to Book a Visit
The best way to experience Harrodian is to see it for yourself. We host regular school tours across all the main entry points, as well as 11+ Open Mornings and a Sixth Form Open Evening. These visits are a great opportunity to explore our beautiful grounds, meet staff and pupils, and ask any questions you may have.
If you are unable to visit in person, you can access our 3D virtual tour by clicking onto the next page via the link below.
Joining Harrodian
How to apply
All applications are completed online via our secure booking system Open Apply. Once registered, you will have access to a personal admissions account where you can:
Track your child’s application
Communicate with our team
Manage contact details
How to register
To register your child, simply click on the button below and provide the following:
A recent photo of your child
End-of-year school report (when available)
Relevant visas (if applicable)
Any additional needs reports (if applicable)
Travelling to Harrodian
Harrodian benefits from a range of accessible and sustainable travel options, including walking, cycling and scooting, as well as excellent public transport links via Barnes Bridge, Barnes and Hammersmith. The area is also well served by local bus routes, and the school offers minibus and coach services. Please note that Hammersmith Bridge is currently closed to vehicles but remains open to pedestrians and cyclists.
Our Entry Process
Click below on relevant entry point to find out more about the process
Academic Achievements and Destinations
Harrodian’s strong, all-round academic reputation continues to grow with excellent results consistently maintaining a steady upward curve across the wide and diverse subject range that is offered at GCSE and A Level.
Pupils' behaviour around school is excellent [...] They enthusiastically participate in their learning.”

Read our most recent Ofsted Reports and other reviews

Discover the ethos and values that underpin Harrodian’s distinctive character and make it a special place to learn, play and grow up.

Welcome To Senior School
Our Senior School prepares pupils for GCSE success while fostering the independence, resilience and maturity they need for the Sixth Form and beyond.
Welcome from the Head of Senior School
Joining the 13s (Year 9) marks a step up for Harrodians. This transition for our pupils is accompanied by a growing emphasis on academic rigour and a parallel focus on philanthropy, volunteering and induction into the Harrodian leadership programme.
Exams naturally become a central focus for our 14s and 15s (Year 10s and 11s) but there are still plenty of opportunities for pupils to express and enjoy themselves on the stage, the sports field and through many other trips and activities.
Head of Senior School
Approach to Learning
Harrodian Senior School provides its pupils with an extensive range of academic opportunities to choose from and explore, and provides them with all the support they need to achieve their full exam potential.
The pastoral and leadership programmes and close ties that the Senior School and Sixth Form pupils have in common ensure that, as they grow towards adulthood, their journey is always underpinned by positive, shared values and a strong spirit of community. ”
Pastoral Care
Their teenage years often present our pupils with significant challenges to navigate. Our Senior School provides the exceptional level of pastoral care and support that every Harrodian needs.
Co-curricular
Harrodian has never believed that teaching and learning should be confined to the classroom. The diversity and scope of our co-curricular clubs, such as STEM and Debating, continue to grow alongside the range of trips that are available, with recent destinations including China and Iceland.
The Arts
The arts have always been an important ingredient in the Harrodian’s academic and cultural life and remain hugely popular co-curricular activities.
Sport
Team spirit is central to Harrodian culture and this is reflected in our steadily improving sporting performance. Across genders and age groups, Harrodian sport is on an upward curve, with full complements of teams consistently competing strongly and successfully.

Welcome To Sixth Form
Set on its own dedicated floor in the Senior building, the Sixth Form is, both literally and metaphorically, the top of our School.
Welcome from the Head of Sixth Form
Harrodian Sixth Form provides outstanding learning and pastoral care within a calm and purposeful environment designed to ensure that our 180 students thrive and achieve their full potential academically and socially.
Good manners, consideration and respect for others are all promoted and commitment to the wider school community is also expected.
Awareness of, and engagement with, the wider world are also both key qualities we develop in our students as they prepare for tertiary education and life as young adults.
Academic
Academic performance and outcomes in the Sixth Form are strong and continuing to steadily improve. We expect students to immerse themselves in their studies and encourage them to aim for the highest levels of attainment, using targets to set an appropriate degree of challenge for every student.
Pastoral Care and Wellbeing
The pastoral care offered in the Sixth Form is instrumental in ensuring every student feels comfortable, cared for and confident about tackling the academic challenges and rigours of A Levels.
Futures: Higher education and careers
The Higher Education support that each student receives at Harrodian is exemplary. The School has a mission to provide the best possible guidance and advice to our Sixth Formers in making degree and career choices and applying to universities and other tertiary institutions.
Co-curricular
Academic life is enriched by many different extra-curricular activities, often with a specific Sixth Form focus. Among the popular choices in the wide range of clubs provided by our staff are Model United Nations, Debating, HAB (Hot Air Ballooning) and CANSAT. We are also always open to the regular suggestions for co-curricular clubs that the students themselves provide.
The pastoral and leadership programmes and close ties that the Senior School and Sixth Form students have in common ensure that, as they grow towards adulthood, their journey is always underpinned by positive, shared values and a strong spirit of community. ”
Students in the Sixth Form develop into successful and mature learners, achieving exceptionally well. ”
Sixth Form students are positive role models for younger pupils”
The Arts
The Arts have long been important ingredients in Harrodian’s academic and cultural life and they remain hugely popular co-curricular activities. We encourage Sixth Formers of all kinds to participate in our Drama, Music and Dance productions and concerts.
Sport
Team spirit is central to Harrodian culture and this is reflected in the rapidly growing strength of our sporting performance. Across all age groups, participation in Harrodian sport is surging with full complements of teams consistently competing strongly and enjoying success in local and regional competitions.

Science with Purpose
Following a recent 9s (Year 5) trip to RHS Garden Wisley, Mr Warren Rodricks reflects on how hands-on learning has helped pupils deepen their understanding of sustainability and their responsibility towards the natural world.
It’s surely our responsibility to do everything within our power to create a planet that provides a home not just for us, but for all life on Earth.”
The study of Science in schools has always sought to inspire young scientists and foster a genuine care for the world around them. To achieve this, it is essential that pupils move beyond the classroom and interact directly with the natural environment itself. With this in mind, our 9s headed outdoors this May to explore, question and discover at RHS Garden Wisley.
As part of this half-term’s Life Cycles topic and in preparation for next half-term’s focus on Sustainability, Wisley provided the perfect setting for pupils to deepen their understanding of the living world and reflect upon their place within it. Surrounded by one of the most diverse and carefully curated gardens in the United Kingdom, the children were encouraged not simply to observe nature, but to think critically about how humans interact with and impact the environment.
As part of this half-term’s Life Cycles topic and in preparation for next half-term’s focus on Sustainability, Wisley provided the perfect setting for pupils to deepen their understanding of the living world and reflect upon their place within it.”
Half of the day was spent participating in a workshop centred on plant variation and the growth process. Pupils explored how plants adapt to different conditions, investigated the factors necessary for healthy growth and considered the extraordinary diversity that exists within the plant kingdom. The workshop provided an engaging blend of scientific investigation, discussion and hands-on learning, allowing pupils to apply their classroom knowledge in a meaningful real-world context.
The remainder of the visit involved a self-guided exploration of the gardens with a particular focus on adaptation and sustainability. From drought-resistant planting to environmentally conscious garden design, pupils were able to see first-hand how science and sustainability work together in practical and innovative ways. Alongside developing their scientific understanding, the trip also encouraged curiosity, independence and thoughtful discussion about the future of our planet.
Most importantly, the visit served as a reminder that Science is not simply a subject confined to laboratories or textbooks. It is a way of understanding the world and recognising our responsibility within it.”

Back in Time
Ours 8s (Year 4) travelled back in time to Ancient Greece as part of a one-night residential trip to historical education centre Ufton Court.
At the beginning of February, our 8s (Year 4) travelled to Ufton Court, a specialist historical education centre, for a one-night residential where they enjoyed a range of activities that supported their history work on the Ancient Greece.
Over two days, the children stepped into the roles of ancient Greek citizens. In the Agora trading game, they exchanged goods with other city states and learnt about the importance of trade. They also explored the role of Hermes, the god of trade, who was known as a ‘divine prankster’. According to Oliver (8OFS), this was his favourite activity. “We were allowed to steal goods in the spirit of Hermes, which was wickedly fun,” he shares.
As a group, they developed a range of everyday survival skills. They built sections of wattle walls using woven sticks, struck sparks from flint to light a fire and ground corn and wheat to make flour. They practised carding, spinning and weaving wool, gaining insight into daily life in Ancient Greece.
Reenactments formed a key part of the programme. The children staged the Battle of Thermopylae and took part in Spartan military manoeuvres using replica weapons. “I really enjoyed the Spartan training game. It felt like we were actually preparing for battle,” says Oliver (8OFS).
A crime and punishment workshop, involving the dramatic sentencing of Mr James Almond, was another memorable session. “Crime and punishment was the best part, especially when we got to act out pushing Mr Almond off a cliff,” says Olivia (8OFS).
During the evening, the children dressed in costume and enjoyed a banquet of chicken, potatoes, bread, fruit and grape juice.
The trip was organised by English and Humanities teacher Ms Kathryn Field, with support from Head of Year Mr James Almond. Reflecting on the visit, Mr Almond said he was extremely impressed by the way the children conducted themselves. For some pupils, it was their first time staying away from home without their families, and he noted that they returned more confident, resilient and independent as a result of the experience.
The residential provided a valuable opportunity for the 8s to bring their classroom learning to life in a fun and interactive way and helped prepare them for longer residential trips as they move up through the Lower Prep.

Bringing History to Life
Our PP2 pupils enjoyed a memorable and immersive day stepping back in time to 1666 for a Great Fire of London workshop.
PP2 pupils enjoyed an immersive and memorable day stepping back in time to 1666 for a Great Fire of London workshop. Dressed in wonderful costumes, the children explored a range of themed stations in the Marquee, including an apothecary, bakery and a scrivener, where they made ink and practised writing with quills.
They also experienced traditional crafts such as weaving, candle making, leatherwork and pewter making all whilst dodging a few cheeky “rats” that caused much excitement and laughter! In the bakery, pupils kneaded dough and learned how Thomas Farriner’s bakery on Pudding Lane may have sparked the Great Fire.
A highlight of the day was the archaeological dig, where pupils sifted through “ashes” to uncover artefacts from the Great Fire.
Our wonderful adult helpers were incredible throughout the day, staying in character to make the experience even more authentic and engaging.
To view more photos, taken by photography intern Yana Kozar, please look at our gallery
It was a joy to see the children so curious, enthusiastic and absorbed in their learning. A truly inspiring day that brought history vividly to life.

After Van Gogh
A visit to a PP3 art class revealed a group of budding artists hard at work on a Van Gogh–inspired project that required both creativity and careful concentration.
There was a striking sense of calm in the PP3 classroom during last week’s painting sessions. With classical music playing softly in the background and every child absorbed in their work, the room felt focused and settled, creating an atmosphere that challenged the usual expectations of Pre-Prep children let loose with paintbrushes!
As part of their expressive painting topic, the children worked in the style of Vincent van Gogh, exploring how feelings and movement can be shown through brushstrokes, colour and texture. They experimented with different ways of applying paint, discovering how small changes in pressure, direction and layering could completely alter the mood of an image.
What stood out most was the level of concentration. Every child was deeply engaged in the process, working quietly and thoughtfully, clearly absorbed in what they were creating. The finished paintings, kept in the pupils’ sketchbooks, will become a very special keepsake for children and their parents, both at the end of the academic year when they can take them home and in years to come

Art in a Classical Setting
Five of our Prep pupils enjoyed practical art making sessions last week in the splendid classical surrounding of Stowe School in Buckinghamshire.
Harrodian took five of its budding artists from the 11s (Year 7) to a special Prep School Art Festival hosted by Stowe School in Buckinghamshire. Teachers and pupils alike were impressed by the Palladian splendour of the school’s classical campus setting and its modern facilities which they explored with the help of former Harrodian teacher Mr Bryn Davies who now is a member of Stowe’s Biology teaching team.
The festival took place in Stowe’s spacious double-height Art Department, where pupils enjoyed three brilliant and productive art-making sessions centred on the theme of landscape. Working across a range of media, they experimented with printmaking, sculpture and pastel collage to create a wonderful collection of both two- and three-dimensional pieces.

Bright Prospects
This summer has already seen an exciting surge of enthusiasm and performance among our girls' cricket teams.
It has been a busy week for girls’ cricket in our 11s (Year 7) upwards.
Last week marked the opening round of the Surrey Cup for both the U12 and U13 teams, with fixtures against strong early-season opposition from Broomwood and Surbiton High School.
Both teams produced highly competitive performances in closely contested matches. Despite their efforts, they were unfortunately knocked out in the first round, with results that could have gone either way.
There was, however, a positive result for the U13 team in the National Schools competition. They delivered an impressive performance to defeat Ibstock at home and now progress to face JAGS in round two, with confidence high following this strong win.
Overall, it has been an encouraging start to the season. Both teams showed resilience, teamwork and clear potential for the matches ahead.
The U14 girls are preparing for their first fixture next Thursday, where they will compete in the opening round of the Surrey Cup. Ms Henson is looking forward to seeing the girls demonstrate their ability in this competition.
Meanwhile, higher up in the Senior School, our U15 team competed in the Surrey “Smash It” competition at Surbiton High School on Monday. This format encourages attacking play and quick running between the wickets, providing valuable experience for the players. The team put these skills into practice on Thursday, securing a comprehensive win against local rivals Kew House. They now look ahead to upcoming fixtures with a focus on continued development through match play.
It is also great to see so many girls playing cricket regularly, both at School and at club level, and performing to a high standard. The girls’ cricket season is looking very promising.
